items.summary: Handoff: retain evidence-needed disposition for fleet security. Fleet-doctor and operations sweeps have no results, so authentication, secrets, isolation, release, dependency, monitoring, incident, TLS, and disclosure controls remain unverified. Ordinary reversible growth is conditional; public exposure and security-sensitive releases remain blocked.

Disposition: evidence_needed for fleet-wide security clearance; blocked for public exposure and security-sensitive releases; conditional for ordinary reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; authentication boundaries, least privilege, secrets handling, container isolation, release provenance and approvals, dependency and supply-chain controls, data exposure, monitoring, incident response, complete TLS posture, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but this does not establish complete TLS coverage. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 35 pass, 14 fail, and 10 unknown, with open banner, consent, analytics, privacy, and terms findings. Retained worker and reviewer failures are containment signals, not evidence of compromise. Risk severity is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, medium for bounded reversible growth. Exact decision: preserve private launch gates and permit only bounded reversible growth that changes no credentials, permissions, dependencies, sensitive data flows, or public security posture; continue existing read-only evidence work only. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

Continue the existing bounded read-only security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated evidence, scope, owners, explicit unknowns, severity, and release implications for access boundaries, secrets, runtime isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, requeue failures, or conduct external outreach.
